chill.title: Dig Through the Scrap Exchange
chill.description: A vast creative-reuse warehouse where industrial offcuts, discontinued stock and genuine oddities are sold by the pound.
chill.bonus: Leave with something under five dollars that you cannot explain.

chill.title: Ride the 1911 Carousel at Pullen Park
chill.description: One of the oldest public parks in the South, with a restored Dentzel carousel, a miniature train and pedal boats on the lake for the price of a coffee.
chill.bonus: Take the pedal boats out and race another pair across the lake.

chill.title: Sprawl on the Weaver Street Lawn in Carrboro
chill.description: The co-op grocery with a front lawn that functions as Carrboro's living room, where a coffee buys you an afternoon.
chill.bonus: Stay long enough to see the lawn turn over completely.

chill.title: Find the Japanese Garden at JC Raulston Arboretum
chill.description: NC State's free research arboretum, ten acres of plants being trialled for the Southeast, including a 300-foot perennial border that peaks in late summer.
chill.bonus: Photograph one plant you have never seen before and look up its name.

chill.title: Linger Over a Cortado at Cocoa Cinnamon
chill.description: Durham's most distinctive coffee bar, tiled and spiced and unhurried, with cardamom and horchata lattes worth ordering over the drip.
chill.bonus: Order the drink the barista recommends rather than your usual.

chill.title: Build a Pastry Box at lucettegrace
chill.description: A contemporary patisserie downtown where the entremets and macarons look like jewellery and taste better than they look.
chill.bonus: Choose six pastries with no repeats and share them properly.

chill.title: Walk the Bean-to-Bar Floor at Videri
chill.description: A working chocolate factory in the Warehouse District where the self-guided tour walks you straight past the winnower and the conches.
chill.bonus: Buy a single-origin bar and taste it before you leave the building.

chill.title: Smell Your Way Through the Raleigh Rose Garden
chill.description: Sixty beds and more than a thousand rose bushes on a terraced slope beside Raleigh Little Theatre, free and almost always quiet.
chill.bonus: Find the most fragrant variety in the garden and remember its name.

chill.title: Lose an Hour in Quail Ridge Books
chill.description: Raleigh's beloved independent bookshop, with staff picks worth trusting and an author event calendar that punches above the city's size.
chill.bonus: Buy whatever book the shelf-talker convinces you to buy.

chill.title: Wander the Terraces at Sarah P. Duke Gardens
chill.description: Fifty-five acres of free gardens on Duke's campus, from the Italianate terraces to a genuinely good Japanese garden with a red bridge.
chill.bonus: Find the koi pond and sit there for fifteen minutes with your phone away.

adventure.title: Loop the Company Mill Trail in Umstead
adventure.description: A 5.8-mile hardwood-forest loop with a creek crossing at an old mill site, ten minutes from the airport and a world away from it.
adventure.bonus: Stop at the mill ruins and skip a stone across Crabtree Creek.

adventure.title: Bike the Neuse River Greenway to the Dam
adventure.description: A 27-mile paved ribbon along the Neuse with boardwalks over wetland and a suspension bridge nobody expects in Raleigh.
adventure.bonus: Ride out to Falls Lake Dam and turn around only when you can see the spillway.

adventure.title: Rip the Singletrack at Lake Crabtree
adventure.description: Tight, rooty, lakeside mountain bike trails that punch well above their elevation, with planes coming in low overhead.
adventure.bonus: Clean a full lap of the Highlander loop without putting a foot down.

adventure.title: Summit Occoneechee Mountain, Then Walk Hillsborough
adventure.description: The highest point in Orange County plus a quarry overlook, ten minutes from a riverwalk and a main street worth the detour.
adventure.bonus: Finish the loop and walk the full Riverwalk into town without driving.

adventure.title: Ride the American Tobacco Trail End to End
adventure.description: Twenty-two miles of converted rail bed running from downtown Durham to Apex, flat enough to talk the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Cross the New Hope Creek bridge without touching the brakes.

adventure.title: Ride the Lake Loop at Harris Lake County Park
adventure.description: Flowy, beginner-forgiving mountain bike trails on a peninsula, with a lake on three sides and a nuclear cooling tower on the horizon.
adventure.bonus: Ride the whole red loop without stopping to check the map.

adventure.title: Night Paddle the Eno with Frog Hollow Outdoors
adventure.description: A guided after-dark canoe run on flat water where the frogs get loud and the only light is whatever the moon gives you.
adventure.bonus: Everyone stops paddling and stays silent for a full minute mid-river.

adventure.title: Scramble Cox Mountain at Eno River State Park
adventure.description: Cross the swinging suspension bridge at Fews Ford and grind up the park's steepest climb for a river view most locals never bother with.
adventure.bonus: Wade into the shallows at Fews Ford before you leave.

adventure.title: Kayak Jordan Lake for Bald Eagles
adventure.description: Jordan Lake holds one of the largest summer bald eagle populations east of the Mississippi, and a kayak puts you under them.
adventure.bonus: Get a photo of an eagle in flight before you take out.

adventure.title: Paddleboard Beaverdam at Falls Lake
adventure.description: The calmest arm of Falls Lake, with a swim beach to collapse on once your legs give out.
adventure.bonus: Paddle out to the far shoreline and back without falling in.

adventure.title: Walk With Lemurs at the Duke Lemur Center
adventure.description: The largest lemur population outside Madagascar, and one summer tour that lets you walk into a forest enclosure while they move through the trees around you.
adventure.bonus: Learn one lemur's name and use it correctly in front of the keeper.

adventure.title: Climb Down to the Raven Rock Overlook
adventure.description: A 150-foot crystalline bluff over the Cape Fear River, reached by a staircase that makes the return trip the real hike.
adventure.bonus: Count the stairs on the way down and get the number right on the way up.

adventure.title: Send Your First V2 at Triangle Rock Club
adventure.description: A big, friendly bouldering and rope gym where the day pass includes shoes and nobody minds that you have never done this.
adventure.bonus: Top out a problem graded at least V2 before you leave.

adventure.title: Meet the Big Cats at Carolina Tiger Rescue
adventure.description: A working sanctuary for tigers, lions and caracals where the guided tour puts you a fence away from animals that were somebody's illegal pet.
adventure.bonus: Book the twilight tour and stay for the sunset roar call.

adventure.title: Swing Through the Canopy at Go Ape Blue Jay Point
adventure.description: Forty-plus obstacles and five zip lines strung through the pines above Falls Lake, with a Tarzan swing you have to commit to.
adventure.bonus: Do the last zip line with no hands.

adventure.title: Catch the Skyline Sunset from Dorothea Dix Park
adventure.description: 308 acres of open hillside with the best unobstructed view of downtown Raleigh, and nobody charges you for it.
adventure.bonus: Bring something to sit on and stay until the streetlights come on.

social.title: Order Off-Menu at Kingfisher
social.description: A dark, low-ceilinged Durham cocktail bar whose drinks are built like tasting menus and whose bartenders will happily go off-script.
social.bonus: Describe a flavour rather than a drink and let them build it.

social.title: Find the Door at Watts & Ward
social.description: A basement prohibition lounge under downtown Raleigh with leather booths, a serious whiskey back bar and no sign on the street.
social.bonus: Order a cocktail off-menu by naming a spirit and a mood.

social.title: Do All Three Nights of Hopscotch
social.description: Raleigh's September festival takes over every club, stage and sidewalk downtown for three days of genre-scrambling sets and late-night shows.
social.bonus: See one band you have never heard of in each of three different venues.

social.title: Descend to Fox Liquor Bar
social.description: Ashley Christensen's basement cocktail room under Beasley's, with more than fifty craft cocktails and the low light to match.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender to make the drink they are most proud of.

social.title: Drink Southern at Fullsteam Tavern
social.description: A brewery built on distinctly Southern ingredients — sweet potato, persimmon, foraged whatever — with a tavern that runs events most nights.
social.bonus: Drink the beer with the strangest ingredient on the board.

social.title: Catch a Show at Motorco Music Hall
social.description: A former car dealership turned mid-size music hall in Durham's Central Park district, with a garage bar attached for before and after.
social.bonus: Get to the front for the headliner rather than hanging at the back.

social.title: Claim a Picnic Table at Ponysaurus
social.description: A Hood Street taproom with a big gravel beer garden, rotating food trucks and live music that spills straight outside.
social.bonus: Stay for whatever is playing in the beer garden, even if you have never heard of them.

social.title: Drink at Raleigh's Newest Brewery, 1323 R&D
social.description: Six industry veterans with a hundred years between them opened this experimental Raleigh taproom, and the board changes constantly.
social.bonus: Order the most experimental thing on the board without asking what is in it.

social.title: Run the Quarter Rack at Boxcar Bar + Arcade
social.description: A warehouse of eighties cabinets, skee-ball and pinball with a full bar and a pizza kitchen, and quarters that go fast.
social.bonus: Beat someone in your group at skee-ball on their own chosen lane.

social.title: Work the Taps at the Raleigh Beer Garden
social.description: A three-storey beer hall on Glenwood South with a tap wall deep enough to have held a world record, and a patio built around a live oak.
social.bonus: Drink one beer brewed within fifty miles and name the brewery.

social.title: See a Band at Cat's Cradle Before They Blow Up
social.description: The club that hosted Nirvana, Pavement and half of indie rock's canon on the way up, still booking four or five nights a week.
social.bonus: Buy the opening act's record at the merch table.

social.title: Sit at the Marble Bar at Alley Twenty Six
social.description: Durham's original craft cocktail room, still cutting its own ice and still the easiest place downtown to start a night.
social.bonus: Order something stirred and clear rather than anything shaken.

foodie.title: Dim Sum, Beer and a Bookshop at Brewery Bhavana
foodie.description: One room that is somehow a dim sum house, a brewery, a florist and a bookstore at once, and pulls all four off.
foodie.bonus: Leave with a book you did not go in for.

foodie.title: Pull Whole Hog at Sam Jones BBQ
foodie.description: Third-generation eastern North Carolina whole-hog barbecue, cooked over wood, served with the vinegar sauce and none of the argument.
foodie.bonus: Order the whole-hog plate and the cornbread, and finish both.

foodie.title: Order the Macaroni au Gratin at Poole's Diner
foodie.description: Ashley Christensen's chalkboard-menu diner has been the centre of gravity for Raleigh dining since 2007, and the macaroni au gratin is the reason.
foodie.bonus: Get a seat at the horseshoe bar rather than a table.

foodie.title: Graze Spanish-Southern Tapas at Mateo
foodie.description: Matt Kelly's tapas bar in the old Book Exchange building, where jamón and pimentón meet North Carolina ingredients without apology.
foodie.bonus: Order at least one plate you cannot pronounce.

foodie.title: Queue for Brisket at Prime Barbecue
foodie.description: A Michelin Bib Gourmand barbecue joint in a Knightdale strip that sells out by mid-afternoon and deserves the drive.
foodie.bonus: Get there before the doors open and be in the first ten people in line.

foodie.title: Shuck a Dozen at St. Roch Fine Oysters
foodie.description: Sunny Gerhart's small downtown oyster bar, a nod to New Orleans without ever pretending to be it.
foodie.bonus: Try one raw oyster with nothing on it at all.

foodie.title: Sit at the Omakase Counter at M Sushi
foodie.description: The Triangle's first serious sushi counter, where Michael Lee's omakase runs course by course in front of you.
foodie.bonus: Eat every piece with your hands, the way the chef intends.

foodie.title: Split a Wood-Fired Pie at Pizzeria Toro
foodie.description: A Durham fixture since 2012, turning out blistered wood-fired pizza and a short list of seasonal snacks from an open kitchen.
foodie.bonus: Order a pie with an ingredient you would normally skip.

foodie.title: Brunch on Bavarian Pastry at Guglhupf
foodie.description: A German bakery and café that has been doing pretzels, rye and a shaded biergarten patio in Durham since 1998.
foodie.bonus: Order the namesake guglhupf cake and take half home.

foodie.title: Beat the Line for a Monuts Biscuit
foodie.description: Ninth Street's doughnut and biscuit counter, where the cake doughnut flavours change daily and the line moves faster than it looks.
foodie.bonus: Try a flavour you have never heard of rather than the one you want.

foodie.title: Eat the Whole Mezze Spread at Ajja
foodie.description: Cheetie Kumar's Five Points room cooks the Mediterranean and the Levant through a Carolina lens, with a wood hearth doing most of the work.
foodie.bonus: Order the whole mezze section for the table and let the kitchen choose the order.

foodie.title: Book the Tasting Menu at Lantern
foodie.description: Andrea Reusing's Franklin Street institution, marrying Asian technique to North Carolina farms and fisheries for over two decades.
foodie.bonus: Stay for a drink in the back bar after dinner.

culture.title: Sit Along the Third-Base Line for the Durham Bulls
culture.description: Minor league baseball with a snorting mechanical bull in left field, cheap beer and the most famous outfield sign in the sport.
culture.bonus: Be there when someone hits the bull and it lights up.

culture.title: See the Contemporary Wing at the Nasher Museum
culture.description: Duke's Rafael Viñoly-designed museum, with a genuinely strong contemporary collection and shows that travel to much bigger cities.
culture.bonus: Pick the one work you would hang at home and argue for it.

culture.title: Stand Under the Duke Chapel Vault
culture.description: A 210-foot Collegiate Gothic tower and a nave of seventy-seven stained glass windows, built in the 1930s and free to walk into.
culture.bonus: Time your visit to catch the carillon.

culture.title: Take the Touring Broadway Night at DPAC
culture.description: One of the busiest theatres in the country by attendance, pulling the big touring Broadway runs into a 2,700-seat room downtown.
culture.bonus: Book the show you know least about.

culture.title: Walk the Slave Dwellings at Historic Stagville
culture.description: One of the largest plantations in the antebellum South, where the surviving quarters built by enslaved carpenters still stand and the tour centres their lives.
culture.bonus: Go on a guided tour rather than walking it alone.

culture.title: Meet the Acrocanthosaurus at the Natural Sciences Museum
culture.description: The largest natural sciences museum in the Southeast, free, with a working research lab you can watch through glass and a dinosaur nobody else has.
culture.bonus: Find the Terror of the South and read the whole placard.

culture.title: Go Loud for the Canes at Lenovo Center
culture.description: The loudest building in the NHL on a good night, where the Carolina Hurricanes play in front of a crowd that treats hockey like a Southern sport.
culture.bonus: Learn the goal song before you go and sing it properly.

culture.title: Stand in Front of the Rodins at the NC Museum of Art
culture.description: A free permanent collection running from Egyptian antiquities to one of the largest Rodin holdings in the country, set in a 164-acre museum park.
culture.bonus: Walk the Blue Loop through the park and find at least three outdoor works.

8ball.title: Eight Ball: One Night, All Three Cities
8ball.description: Drink in Raleigh, see a show in Durham, end the night at a Chapel Hill diner counter — the whole Triangle in one run, no backtracking allowed.
8ball.bonus: Do the entire thing without opening a maps app more than twice.

8ball.title: Eight Ball: Trail, Then Whatever Is Closest
8ball.description: Ride the American Tobacco Trail as far as your legs allow, then eat at the first place you pass on the way back — no reviews, no debate.
8ball.bonus: Order the thing the person behind the counter recommends.
